findings.title: CLI verification assumes an enforcement path the design does not establish
findings.description:
The design promises that a CLI invocation produces a threshold-derived verdict, but its documented enforcement contract operates through `ReviewAction` and returns an `ActionResult`. Slice 301 likewise establishes enforcement at that action boundary, not a shared CLI boundary. The walkthrough also expects the derived verdict to be persisted without explaining how it reaches persistence.

Use a pipeline review step for the required end-to-end verification, or explicitly resolve CLI and persistence integration. Deferring the command syntax alone (lines 376–379) does not resolve this contract gap.

findings.title: Failure mapping omits required ground-truth and transport cases
findings.description:
The table covers missing registry inputs, but not an input path resolving successfully to an unreadable/missing ground-truth file, or injected ground truth exceeding the cap. Both are explicitly enumerated by the architecture’s “Failure modes and their verdict mapping” commitment. A hung request and peer disconnect mid-response also lack explicit handling strategies.

Document how these cases terminate with an observable, non-passing outcome, including the inherited timeout/cancellation mechanism. Existing handling can be referenced; new machinery is unnecessary. A general claim that infrastructure handles every case does not establish these mappings.
